title: Seeded CSS encoder and propagated-fault verification synthesis
difficulty_explanation: A solution must synthesize compact H/CNOT encoders from scrambled CSS generators, enumerate the complete declared circuit-level Pauli fault model, quotient final errors by the target-state stabilizer, reproduce TensorCircuit fault syndromes, and solve a seeded lexicographic minimum set-cover problem for both 7- and 15-qubit instances.
solution_explanation: The reference implementation row-reduces the hidden X space, executes the encoder and every dangerous final Pauli representative with TensorCircuit, obtains candidate-check expectations with Circuit.expectation_ps, and selects the exact minimum verification cover.
verification_explanation: The evaluator never imports TensorCircuit. It independently propagates binary symplectic stabilizers and Pauli faults, computes target-state coset distance, reconstructs every candidate syndrome, and exhaustively proves the lexicographic optimum.
relevant_experience: The prototype is based on CSS logical-zero preparation, Clifford fault propagation, and stabilizer-check verification under a fully enumerated encoder-fault model.

contract.anti_hardcoding: The seed changes the 7- and 15-qubit permutations, generator bases, candidate stabilizers, candidate identifiers, and pool order. The submitted encoder determines the fault ensemble checked by the independent oracle.
contract.oracle: Independent GF(2) row-space checks, an exact 2^15-amplitude sign canary, binary symplectic Clifford propagation, target-state stabilizer coset distance, and exhaustive set-cover optimization

difficulty_levers: scrambled CSS generator bases instead of a named-code circuit
both 7-qubit and 15-qubit quantum Hamming logical-zero states
all nonidentity Pauli faults after every encoder H and CNOT
state-stabilizer quotient before classifying a fault as dangerous
TensorCircuit check expectations for every dangerous error
seeded exact lexicographic minimum stabilizer-check cover
claim_boundary: The declared model covers preparation X faults and all Pauli faults on encoder gates, with ideal nondestructive verification checks. It does not claim fault tolerance of the check-measurement gadgets themselves. No solver-model trial has been run.
api_risks: Circuit.expectation_ps uses ps codes 0=I, 1=X, 2=Y, 3=Z in the pinned image; a convention change corrupts the syndrome matrix.
TensorCircuit qubit indices follow the state tensor-axis order used by Circuit gates, while the independent oracle treats index zero as the first symplectic coordinate.
TensorCircuit backend and dtype setters are process-global, so the expert sets NumPy/complex128 explicitly.
expectation_ps contraction reuse and floating-point signs should be canaried after TensorCircuit upgrades; the prototype thresholds signs at -0.5 with ideal values near plus or minus one.
